content:
Xanatos Prime said
....... That being said - is there a more appropriate place to leave a note regarding the particular Mozilla Support article https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/calendar-updates-issues-thunderbird with which I had issues? I do note on revisiting it that its last reported revision was way back in 2018, and that that article is so specifically on point that it's probably getting a fair number of views from other CardBook users right now....

It is out of date. The Calendar used to be an addon called Lightning, but that is no longer the case. The Calendar is now an integral part of Thunderbird. The language used throughout the article is obviously out of date.

But your issue is not due to a bug specifically in the Thunderbird Calendar which would need fixing by Thunderbird developers due to a bug, it's caused by an add-on called Cardbook which is inserting it's own bits of code. When Thunderbird makes an update, the authors of add-ons are having to check their add-on continues to function, so they are always in catch up mode. Those authors do not get any monies from Thunderbird, they rely on people donating monies to support the add-on they use, thus enabling the authors to have time to do the necessary code changes and tests. You would be surprised how many people use add-ons expect them to keep up to date but do not contribute to their upkeep. In the past, I've known many authors just stop updating add-ons, Sometimes they do not have the time to learn new code or the time to work on the constant updates or they lose interest. It takes a lot of time and effort.

You may be aware that unpaid volunteers offer their time to help people in this Support Forum and a similar case occurs with all Help Articles. It relies on people having the time to update them. In recent years there has been so many changes that it's not been possible to keep up. I know I decided not to do some because I was waiting for all changes to occur otherwise I would be editing on a constant basis.

If anyone ever has an issue and they use any add-on, the first thing they should try is using Troubleshoot mode or manually disable all add-ons. I think you would probably find that in thousands of comments posted because it is used as a basic test and starting point to track down or rule out potential causes.

In Thunderbird

  • Help > Troubleshoot mode
  • click on Restart and then select 'Continue in Troubleshoot Mode'

If you use add-ons, I suggest you do not use the Auto update option.

  • Settings > General
  • scroll to Updates section
  • Select 'Check for updates, but let me choose whether to install them'

That means when you check 'Help' > 'About Thunderbird', it will tell you if another version is available. That then gives you time to check all the add-ons you use. Look on the download page for that add-on and see what comments have been posted. Some add-ons also have links to their own Support page where you may find info. Basically, it gives you a bit of breathing space to check things out and delay the update if required.

Best advise I can offer is if you use Add-ons, use the ESR version of Thunderbird as it gets major updates on a less frequent basis. So, in theory, issues with add-ons would have been previously noted and fixed before you use the version where they would have failed. But it always says 'May not work with all add-ons'.

Info shown on the download webpage. The official Thunderbird Release channel. This release is intended for users who want all available new features and bug fixes on a monthly basis. May not work with all add-ons.

The official Extended Support Release channel. This release is intended for users who want all available new features on an annual basis and stability/security fixes on a monthly basis. May not work with all add-ons.

content:
It does not appear like Thunderbird has proper support for mailboxes that are no longer available.

With IMAP there is no concept of a local offline account. To preserve your messages you should have copied your messages from the IMAP account to the Local Folders account, while the account still existed on the IMAP server.

Local folders would not really help in this situation either, unless you plan out exactly when your mailbox goes offline.

Isn't that would you did by deliberately deleting the account on the IMAP server? That's different from a server being not reachable for whatever reason. But even then accidents can happen. This is what backups are for. For local backups to work in connection with an IMAP account you'll have to turn on 'Synchronization' in Thunderbird. That's Thunderbird speak for downloading an offline copy of all messages on the server to your local disk. https://support.mozilla.org/kb/imap-synchronization
